mainTopic: Food left on a כירה over שבת: שוגג versus מזיד, the גזרה against one who forgets, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the penalty for one who wrongly leaves a pot, and the start of returning a pot (חזרה)
overview: Someone asks רבי חייא בר אבא about a pot that was forgotten on a כירה and cooked on שבת. The next day he teaches publicly: one who cooks on שבת בשוגג may eat, במזיד may not, "and it is no different." רבה and רב יוסף read this leniently, so even במזיד the pot's food may be eaten. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads it strictly, so even בשוגג it is forbidden. A ברייתא that permits שוגג and forbids מזיד fits רב נחמן בר יצחק if it was taught before a גזרה. It stays a קשיא against רבה and רב יוסף. רב explains the גזרה: once people began leaving pots on purpose and claiming they forgot, חכמים penalized even the one who truly forgot. The גמרא resolves apparent contradictions in רבי מאיר (לכתחילה versus דיעבד) and רבי יהודה (a גרופה וקטומה stove versus one that is not). It then asks whether someone who wrongly left a pot is penalized. A proof from רבי יוסי in ציפורי is rejected, and a story confirms that shriveled eggs improve with more cooking. Finally the גמרא turns to בית הלל's ruling that one may even return a pot, and רב ששת's statement on this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The question: a pot forgotten on the stove that cooked on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא is asked about a pot that was forgotten on a כירה before שבת and then cooked on שבת. May the food be eaten?
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone forgot a pot on top of a stove and it cooked on שבת, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A question is being asked: if a pot was left on the stove before שבת and it finished cooking on שבת, may you eat the food? This sets up everything that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person did not cook anything on שבת with his own hands. The fire did the cooking while the pot sat there. So the question is whether this kind of passive cooking forbids the food the way active cooking on שבת does.

keyTerms.meaning: He forgot (here: left the pot on the fire before שבת)
A stove with spaces for two pots

steps.confusionAlert: "Forgot" does not mean he forgot about שבת. It means he left the pot on a כירה before שבת in a way that is not allowed (for example, without sweeping out or covering the coals). The later terms שוגג and מזיד describe whether he left it there by mistake or on purpose.

phrases.english: One forgot a pot on top of a stove
and it cooked on Shabbat; what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁכַח קְדֵירָה עַל גַּבֵּי כִּירָה וּבִשְּׁלָהּ בְּשַׁבָּת, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion here; it continues the earlier topic of leaving pots on a כירה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether food that cooked on שבת in a pot forgotten on the כירה may be eaten.

steps.title: Silence, then a public teaching the next day
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא does not answer at first. The next day he publicly teaches: one who cooks on שבת בשוגג may eat, במזיד may not eat, "and it is no different."
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent and said nothing at all. The next day he went out and taught them: One who cooks on שבת, if by mistake he may eat; if on purpose he may not eat; and it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering right away, the רב waits and then teaches the general rule about cooking on שבת. He adds the unclear phrase "ולא שנא" (it is no different), which seems to connect the rule to the forgotten pot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is clear: food cooked on שבת by mistake may be eaten, and food cooked on purpose may not. The added phrase "ולא שנא" hints that for the forgotten pot, there is no difference between שוגג and מזיד. It does not say whether that means both are permitted or both are forbidden, and the גמרא asks about that next.

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: He was silent and did not say anything to him at all.
The next day he went out and taught them:
One who cooks on Shabbat:
if unwittingly, he may eat it;
if intentionally, he may not eat it;
and it is no different.
phrases.notes: This vague phrase is what the גמרא will analyze next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1, but indirectly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cooking בשוגג: may eat. Cooking במזיד: may not eat. The forgotten pot is "no different," though the meaning is unclear.

steps.title: What does "it is no different" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the phrase "ולא שנא".
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "and it is no different" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what that unclear phrase means. This is a setup line, and two different explanations come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "No different" could mean the forgotten pot is no different in a lenient way or no different in a strict way. The גמרא needs to know which one before it can give the law for the forgotten pot.

phrases.english: What is meant by "and it is no different"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to clarify the final phrase of step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether "ולא שנא" is meant leniently or strictly regarding the forgotten pot.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: the lenient reading
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף explain that only active cooking במזיד forbids the food. Leaving a pot on the fire is not an action, so the food may be eaten even if it was left there on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said it leniently: one who cooks is doing an action, so if on purpose he may not eat. But this person, who did not do an action, may eat even if he did it on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer reads "ולא שנא" leniently. The forgotten pot is permitted whether it was left by mistake or on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is מעשה, a real action. Someone who cooks on שבת actively does something forbidden, so the penalty for doing it on purpose applies. Someone who only left a pot sitting did no act on שבת, so even במזיד there is no penalty. On this reading, "no different" means שוגג and מזיד are no different for him: both may eat.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ לְהֶיתֵּירָא:
phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both said it in the lenient direction:
It is one who cooks, who performs an action,
who, if intentionally, may not eat;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַאי דְּלָא קָא עָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה —
phrases.english: but this one, who does not perform an action,
even intentionally may eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ לְהֶיתֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lenient: no action was done, so even במזיד the food may be eaten.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the strict reading
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that one who leaves a pot might trick others by claiming he forgot it. So the food is forbidden even בשוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said it strictly: a cook will not try to trick anyone, so if by mistake he may eat. But this person might come to trick, so even by mistake he may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The second answer reads "ולא שנא" strictly. The forgotten pot is forbidden whether it was left by mistake or on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is איערומי, scheming. Nobody would openly cook on שבת and then claim it was an accident, so a real שוגג cook is believed. But a person could leave a pot on purpose and later say "I forgot." So חז"ל forbade the food even when he truly forgot. Here "no different" means both cases are forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק is not saying the person who forgot did something wrong. It is a protective rule: since other people could lie about forgetting, the food is forbidden even for the one who really forgot.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two readings stand at opposite extremes: permitted even במזיד, or forbidden even בשוגג. Both will be challenged by the ברייתא that comes next.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר לְאִיסּוּרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said it in the strict direction:
It is one who cooks, who will not come to scheme,
who, if unwittingly, may eat;
but this one, who may come to scheme,
even unwittingly may not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר לְאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite interpretation to step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Strict: because of the worry about deception, even בשוגג the food is forbidden.

steps.title: A baraita: the mistake versus on-purpose distinction, and רבי מאיר's limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says about a forgotten pot: בשוגג may eat, במזיד may not. רבי מאיר limits this to food not fully cooked; fully cooked food may be eaten either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If one forgot a pot on a stove and it cooked on שבת, by mistake he may eat; on purpose he may not. When is this said? With water not fully heated and food not fully cooked. But water fully heated and food fully cooked, whether by mistake or on purpose, he may eat. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the two explanations with a ברייתא. It says that for a forgotten pot, the law does depend on שוגג or מזיד, at least for food that was not fully cooked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא distinguishes שוגג from מזיד in the forgotten-pot case. רבה and רב יוסף said even מזיד may eat, and רב נחמן בר יצחק said even שוגג may not eat, so the ברייתא seems to contradict both. רבי מאיר adds that the whole distinction only applies when the food still needed cooking. Fully cooked food may be eaten in either case.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
In what case is this said? (limits the ruling)
Fully, as much as it needs

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who forgot a pot on top of a stove
and it cooked on Shabbat:
if unwittingly, he may eat; if intentionally, he may not eat.
In what case is this said?
With hot water that was not fully heated
and a dish that was not fully cooked;
but hot water that was fully heated
and a dish that was fully cooked,
whether unwittingly or intentionally, he may eat;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges both interpretations of "ולא שנא" given in steps 4 and 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lenient reading of רבה and רב יוסף and the strict reading of רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly distinguishes שוגג (may eat) from מזיד (may not eat) for a forgotten pot. That contradicts "even מזיד may eat" and also "even שוגג may not eat."

steps.title: רבי יהודה: does the food improve or get worse as it shrinks?
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the ברייתא, רבי יהודה says fully heated water is permitted because shrinking ruins it. Fully cooked food is forbidden because shrinking improves it. He then gives the general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Water that was fully heated is permitted because it shrinks and is worse for it. A dish that was fully cooked is forbidden because it shrinks and is better for it. Anything that shrinks and improves, like cabbage, beans, and chopped meat, is forbidden; anything that shrinks and gets worse is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the same ברייתא. רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי מאיר about fully cooked food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the question is whether the person still benefits from more cooking. If the food gets better as it shrinks (cabbage, beans, chopped meat), he has a reason to want it on the fire, and we worry he might stoke the coals, so it is forbidden. If it only gets worse (water evaporating), he has no such reason, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is bad for it (it gets worse)
And it is good for it (it improves)

steps.whatToRemember: In this ברייתא, רבי מאיר says fully cooked food may be eaten whether left בשוגג or במזיד. רבי יהודה says it depends: food that improves as it shrinks is forbidden, and food that gets worse is permitted. The גמרא's challenge to רבה and רב יוסף and to רב נחמן בר יצחק comes from the opening ruling about food not fully cooked (בשוגג may eat, במזיד may not), as Step 8 points out.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of מצטמק ויפה לו versus מצטמק ורע לו becomes a central tool in the הלכות of leaving food on the fire for שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Hot water that was fully heated is permitted
because it shrinks and that is bad for it.
And a dish that was fully cooked is forbidden
because it shrinks and that is good for it.
And anything that shrinks and improves,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן כְּרוּב וּפוֹלִים וּבָשָׂר טָרוּף — אָסוּר,
phrases.english: such as cabbage, beans, and chopped meat, is forbidden;
and anything that shrinks and gets worse is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 6 with רבי יהודה's dissenting view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fully cooked food that improves as it shrinks is forbidden; anything that gets worse as it shrinks (such as fully heated water) is permitted.

steps.title: Focusing on the ruling for food that was not fully cooked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the part of the ברייתא about food that was not fully cooked. That ruling is: בשוגג may eat, במזיד may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches a ruling about food that was not fully cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It highlights one piece of the ברייתא from Step 6 so it can test it against the earlier explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For food that was not fully cooked, the ברייתא says בשוגג is permitted and במזיד is forbidden. This sits between the two earlier opinions. רב נחמן בר יצחק forbids even בשוגג, while רבה and רב יוסף permit even במזיד. So both opinions look challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. Used to zoom in on the part of a source that matters for the challenge.
Fully, as much as it needs

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches
food that was not fully cooked
phrases.notes: For this food: בשוגג may eat, במזיד may not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא from Step 6 to use it as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations of רב נחמן בר יצחק and of רבה ורב יוסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's middle position (שוגג permitted, מזיד forbidden) fits neither opinion as it stands.

steps.title: No problem for רב נחמן בר יצחק: before and after the decree
steps.stepSummary: For רב נחמן בר יצחק there is no difficulty. The ברייתא was taught before the גזרה, and his ruling reflects the law after the גזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out fine for רב נחמן בר יצחק. The ברייתא was taught before the decree, and his ruling is after the decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב נחמן בר יצחק can explain the ברייתא without trouble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the גזרה, a forgotten pot was treated like ordinary cooking: שוגג permitted, מזיד forbidden. That is exactly what the ברייתא says. Later, חכמים made a גזרה forbidding even שוגג, and that is the law רב נחמן בר יצחק describes.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for... Introduces the side that has no problem, before turning to the side that does.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak
it is not difficult:
here, before the decree,
there, after the decree.
phrases.notes: Refers to רב נחמן בר יצחק's ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לָרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 8 on behalf of רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different time periods (before and after a decree)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to contradict רב נחמן בר יצחק, since it permits שוגג.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reflects the law before the גזרה. רב נחמן בר יצחק reflects the law after it.

steps.title: Challenge to רבה and רב יוסף from either time period
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף permit even במזיד. If the ברייתא is from before the גזרה, its ban on מזיד contradicts them. If we are speaking about after the גזרה, the law then forbids even שוגג, so their permission is contradicted in the שוגג case too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for רבה and רב יוסף, who read it leniently: if the ברייתא is from before the decree, its ruling on מזיד is a problem. If it is from after the decree, its ruling on שוגג is also a problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the 'before/after' answer cannot save רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה and רב יוסף say leaving a pot is never forbidden, even במזיד. Before the גזרה, the ברייתא still forbids מזיד, which already contradicts them. After the גזרה, even שוגג would be forbidden, which is even further from their view. So neither time period works for them.

keyTerms.meaning: If... if... Sets up a two-sided trap where both options fail.

phrases.english: But Rabbah and Rav Yosef,
who read it leniently,
if it is before the decree, the ruling on intentional is difficult.
If it is after the decree,
the ruling on unintentional is also difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי לְהֶיתֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רב נחמן בר יצחק, who has an answer, to רבה ורב יוסף, who do not.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבה ורב יוסף that leaving a pot is permitted even במזיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma: in either time period, the ברייתא forbids something they permit.

steps.title: The challenge stands unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes 'קשיא': the problem for רבה and רב יוסף remains unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer for רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain 'קשיא' means the question is left open and the opinion is weakened. It is not a full rejection like 'תיובתא'. Still, רב נחמן בר יצחק's view now stands on firmer ground.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. The question remains unanswered.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא fits רב נחמן בר יצחק, using the before/after גזרה split. For רבה and רב יוסף it remains a קשיא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from Step 10 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה ורב יוסף's lenient reading remains challenged by the ברייתא.

steps.title: What was the decree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what גזרה was meant by 'before and after the decree.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the decree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask which decree it has been talking about. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 9 relied on a גזרה that was never explained. Now the גמרא asks for its content.

phrases.english: What is the decree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of the גזרה mentioned in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The content and history of the גזרה

steps.title: רב's account: penalizing the one who forgets
steps.stepSummary: At first, the cooking rule (שוגג may eat, מזיד may not) applied equally to one who forgot a pot. When people began leaving pots on purpose and claiming they forgot, חכמים penalized even the one who truly forgot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: At first they would say that if one cooks on שבת by mistake, he may eat it, and if on purpose, he may not. The same applied to one who forgot a pot. When many people began leaving pots on purpose and saying 'We forgot,' חכמים went back and penalized the one who forgot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a chain of teachers going back to רב, who describes how the law changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally, forgetting a pot was treated like cooking בשוגג, so the food was permitted. Because people abused the 'I forgot' excuse, חכמים made a קנס (penalty) that forbids the food even for someone who truly forgot. This is the גזרה behind רב נחמן בר יצחק's ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic reason for a rabbinic decree: closing a loophole that people were exploiting, even though it means a stricter rule for honest people.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda bar Shmuel said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Abba said that Rav Kahana said that Rav said:
At first they would say:
one who cooks on Shabbat,
by mistake, may eat;
on purpose, may not eat;
and the same applies to one who forgets.
Once many began leaving pots on purpose
and saying, 'We forgot,'
they went back and penalized one who forgets.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גזרה was a קנס on one who forgot a pot, because people falsely claimed to have forgotten.

steps.title: Contradictions within רבי מאיר and within רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Each תנא's view in this ברייתא seems to contradict his own view in the earlier ברייתא about בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר contradicts רבי מאיר, and רבי יהודה contradicts רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה seem to say opposite things in two different sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי מאיר forbade leaving food on the stove even according to בית הלל, yet here he permits fully cooked food even במזיד. Earlier, רבי יהודה said בית הלל permit leaving food, yet here he forbids fully cooked food because shrinking improves it.

keyTerms.meaning: A contradiction between one statement of a sage and another statement of the same sage

steps.confusionAlert: The 'other' statements are not here. They come from the earlier ברייתא at the start of the פרק, about בית שמאי and בית הלל.

phrases.english: There is a contradiction between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Meir,
there is a contradiction between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to an internal problem in the ברייתא quoted in Steps 6-7.
steps.kashyaTarget: Consistency of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה across two sources
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each sage seems lenient in one source and strict in the other on the same topic.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: before the fact versus after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר forbids leaving food at the outset (לכתחילה). He permits eating it once it was already left (דיעבד).
steps.simpleTranslation: Between רבי מאיר and רבי מאיר there is no contradiction. This one is about what to do at the outset, and that one is about after it has already happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction in רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two statements address different questions. One asks whether you may leave the pot at all, and the answer is no. The other asks whether you may eat the food once it was left, and the answer is yes.

phrases.english: Between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Meir
there is no contradiction:
this is at the outset, that is after the fact.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אַדְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר is both strict and lenient about the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is strict about leaving the pot, and lenient about eating the food afterward.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a swept and covered stove versus one that is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה permits leaving food on a stove that is גרופה וקטומה (coals swept out or covered with ash). He forbids it on a stove that is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between רבי יהודה and רבי יהודה there is also no contradiction. Here it is a stove that was swept or covered with ash, and there it is a stove that was not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction in רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two statements describe different stoves. When the coals are removed or covered, there is less concern that someone will stir them, so leaving the pot is allowed. When the coals are left as they are, it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Swept out, with the coals removed
Covered with ash, so the coals are smothered

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: strict לכתחילה, lenient דיעבד. רבי יהודה: lenient on a גרופה וקטומה stove, strict on one that is not.

phrases.english: Between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yehuda
there is also no contradiction:
here, with a swept and ash-covered stove,
there, with one that is not swept and ash-covered.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה both permits and forbids leaving food on the stove.
steps.terutzMaskana: He permits it on a גרופה וקטומה stove and forbids it on one that is not.

steps.title: If one left a pot against the rules, was he penalized?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if someone broke the rule and left a pot on the fire, did חכמים forbid him to eat the food?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If someone violated the rule and left the pot, what is the law? Did חכמים penalize him or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the penalty for someone who knowingly left a pot where he should not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know leaving the pot was forbidden. The new question is about the consequence: is the food itself now forbidden as a קנס, or only the act?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them. Introduces an open question.
He violated the rule and left the pot on the fire

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
If he violated the rule and left it, what is the law?
Did the Sages penalize him, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that leaving a pot is forbidden, and asks about the penalty.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether food left on the fire against the rules becomes forbidden to eat

steps.title: Proof from רבי יוסי in ציפורי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי allowed hot water that had been left on the stove, but forbade shriveled eggs that had been left there. The גמרא suggests this was a ban on eating them that same שבת, which would prove there is a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: when רבי יוסי went to ציפורי, he found hot water left on the stove and did not forbid it to them. He found shriveled eggs left on the stove and forbade them. Isn't this about that same שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that seems to answer the question with 'yes, they were penalized.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי treated hot water and shriveled eggs differently, which suggests the eggs were left in a forbidden way. If he forbade eating the eggs that very שבת, that would prove חכמים penalize food that was left against the rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. Introduces a proof.
Is it not? Suggests a reading of the source.

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נָתָן אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: as Shmuel bar Natan said that Rabbi Chanina said:
When Rabbi Yosei went to Tzippori,

phrases.aramaic: מָצָא חַמִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּהוּ עַל גַּבֵּי כִּירָה
phrases.english: he found hot water that had been left on a stove
and he did not forbid it to them;

phrases.aramaic: בֵּיצִים מְצוּמָּקוֹת שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּהוּ עַל גַּבֵּי כִּירָה,
phrases.english: shriveled eggs that had been left on a stove,
and he forbade them to them.
Is this not referring to that same Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נָתָן אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question of Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים penalized one who left a pot against the rules
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ruling in ציפורי about the eggs

steps.title: No, the ban was for the following Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. רבי יוסי only forbade leaving eggs that way in the future. He did not forbid eating the eggs that Shabbat.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, he forbade it for the next Shabbat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'He forbade them' can mean he told people not to leave eggs on the stove from now on. It does not have to mean the eggs already left were forbidden to eat. So the story does not prove there is a קנס, and the question remains open.

phrases.english: No, for the following Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 18.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban may refer only to future שבתות, not to eating the food already left.

steps.title: Do shriveled eggs actually improve with more cooking?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי יוסי's ruling that shriveled eggs get better the longer they cook. It asks, with some surprise, whether this is really true.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we learn from this that shriveled eggs keep shriveling, and that this is good for them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices something implied by רבי יוסי's split between hot water and eggs. It asks whether eggs really improve when they keep cooking and shrivel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allowed leaving hot water but not shriveled eggs. That split only makes sense if longer cooking helps the eggs. Then a person would want them to cook more and might stir the coals. The גמרא is surprised by this, since overcooked eggs sound ruined, so it checks the assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: From the implication of; we can infer that
Shriveled eggs, cooked down until they shrink
It is good for them; it improves them

phrases.english: Can we infer that shriveled eggs
phrases.notes: Drawn from רבי יוסי's ruling in the previous step

phrases.english: keep shriveling, and it is good for them?
phrases.notes: Asked with surprise. Normally overcooking ruins food.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּבֵיצִים מְצוּמָּקוֹת מִצְטַמְּקוֹת וְיָפֶה לָהֶן נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוסי's ruling about eggs (steps 18-19). It asks about the factual reason behind the ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether shriveled eggs really improve with extended cooking, which would explain why רבי יוסי forbade leaving them on the stove.

steps.title: Yes — the story of רב חמא בר חנינא and רבי eating shriveled eggs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, and supports it with a story. רב חמא בר חנינא and רבי were served eggs shriveled to the size of crab apples, and they ate many of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. As רב חמא בר חנינא said: One time רבי and I were guests at a certain place. They brought us eggs shriveled down like crab apples, and we ate a lot of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes: shriveled eggs really do improve. It proves this with a story about important rabbis enjoying them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If great rabbis ate many of these eggs, they must have tasted good. So people want eggs to keep shriveling. That explains why רבי יוסי worried that someone would stir the coals to cook them more.

keyTerms.meaning: Like crab apples (small, hard fruit), describing the eggs' shrunken size

steps.whyThisMatters: This confirms the reason behind רבי יוסי's ruling. Food that improves with more cooking creates a real fear that someone will stir the coals on שבת.

phrases.english: Yes.
phrases.notes: Direct answer: overcooking does improve the eggs

phrases.english: As Rav Ḥama bar Ḥanina said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת נִתְאָרַחְתִּי אֲנִי וְרַבִּי לִמְקוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: One time Rabbi and I were guests at a certain place
and they brought before us eggs shriveled like crab apples
and we ate many of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין דְּאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 20 and gives a story as proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, shriveled eggs improve with extended cooking, as shown by רב חמא בר חנינא and רבי eating many of them.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי forbade leaving shriveled eggs on the stove because they get better as they shrink. That creates a worry someone will stir the coals. Hot water does not improve that way, so it was permitted.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: בית הלל allow even returning a pot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. בית הלל say one may even return a pot to the stove on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: One may even return (the pot to the stove).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. It is setting up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was leaving food on the stove from before שבת. Now the topic moves to returning a pot to the stove on שבת after it was taken off. The word 'אף' (even) shows that בית הלל go further than just allowing food to stay.

keyTerms.meaning: One may return (a pot to the stove)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Returning' (חזרה) is a different action from 'leaving' (שהייה). Leaving means the pot stays on the stove from before שבת. Returning means putting it back on שבת after it was removed.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say: one may even return [the pot].
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing the topic of חזרה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the שהייה discussion to the next clause of the משנה, about returning a pot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, one may even return a pot to the stove on שבת.

steps.title: רב ששת begins a statement about returning a pot
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת begins a ruling about returning a pot, framed around a certain opinion. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: According to the one who says...
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts to explain בית הלל's rule about returning a pot. This line is only the opening, and his full statement comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לדברי האומר' means 'according to the opinion that holds...'. רב ששת is about to tie the returning rule to one side of an earlier argument. We have to wait for the next passage to see which opinion he means and what he rules.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says (introduces a specific opinion)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: According to the one who says
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the אמורא's explanation of the משנה line quoted in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incomplete on this amud. רב ששת begins to limit or explain the returning rule according to a specific opinion.
